principles: Derive every figure number deterministically from the raw records; never hand-transcribe
Reuse the existing dedup + outcome semantics (adjudicate-produced adjudicatedOutcome) — the generator counts, it does not re-classify
Offline + zero new dependencies — plain Node emitting a standalone SVG, testable without the campaign data
Single responsibility: this generator only reads records and draws; CI/statistics stay in analyze.mjs
drivers: Reproducibility: the committed-generator norm requires rebuilding the figure from powered/*.jsonl
Offline determinism: the selfcheck must run in npm test with synthetic records and no LLM
Non-interference: do not touch the paper, adjudicate.mjs, analyze.mjs, or the campaign data

options.name: Standalone Node generator emitting SVG+CSV, with a synthetic-record offline selfcheck
pros: No new deps; matches the repo (all recovery-runner tooling is .mjs)
Deterministic + offline-testable via injected synthetic records
SVG is vector, converts to PDF for the paper; CSV makes numbers auditable
Counts only, delegates classification to the records adjudicate already produced
cons: Re-implements a small dedup that also lives in analyze (must keep the keep-first key identical)

options.name: Extend analyze.mjs to also emit the figure
pros: Single pass; dedup shared with the stats
cons: Bloats the locked analysis script + risks regressing its CI/GLMM output
Mixes plotting into the statistics module (two responsibilities)
Harder to keep the figure generator a small auditable unit

options.name: Python + matplotlib generator
cons: Adds a Python/matplotlib toolchain dependency the repo does not have
Inconsistent with the all-Node recovery-runner tooling

chosen: Standalone Node generator emitting SVG+CSV, with a synthetic-record offline selfcheck
rationale: A small standalone Node generator matches the all-.mjs recovery-runner tooling, adds no dependencies, and stays offline-testable with synthetic records — the same discipline every existing selfcheck follows. It counts outcomes already assigned by adjudicate (no re-classification) and leaves the bootstrap CI in analyze.mjs, keeping responsibilities clean. The only care point is that its keep-first dedup key must be byte-identical to analyze's; a selfcheck asserts the counts so drift is caught.

preMortem.scenario: Dedup key drifts from analyze.mjs so the figure double-counts restart duplicates
preMortem.trigger: using a different key tuple or not deduping
preMortem.consequence: per-arm counts diverge from the paper stats (e.g. 9,317 vs 9,240)
preMortem.mitigation: use the exact arm|taskId|scenarioId|repeat keep-first key; the selfcheck feeds duplicate synthetic records and asserts they are collapsed

preMortem.scenario: The generator silently reads *.voids.jsonl sidecars as records
preMortem.consequence: void entries pollute the denominator / counts
preMortem.mitigation: explicitly exclude *.voids.jsonl; the selfcheck includes a voids-like file and asserts it is ignored

preMortem.scenario: The new selfcheck is not picked up by the aggregator
preMortem.trigger: missing final summary line or not added to run-selfchecks SELFCHECKS array
preMortem.consequence: npm test does not actually exercise the generator
preMortem.mitigation: print a final "…assertions passed" line matching the aggregator regex and add the file to the SELFCHECKS array; verify run-selfchecks reports 8
